newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks end lower, losing streak goes on.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks end lower, losing streak goes on.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended slightly lower after a day of lackluster trade in which taxes were cited among reasons the market has failed to follow through on its spectacular gains earlier this month.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index slipped a razor-thin 0.01 percent to close at 14,879.00 on a trading volume of 2.02 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB fell 0.10 percent, meanwhile, ending at 957.78. Volume in the capital was 1.3 billion.

Market analysts said share prices generally appeared to have stabilized after falling across-the-board for nine consecutive trading sessions. But there were fears that the government's decision to eliminate income tax exemptions for capital gains stemming from stocks would continue weighing on equities.
Carlos Caballero, president of the Bogota stock exchange, protested against the measure in an open letter Monday to

Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo. Announced last week as part of the government's effort to broaden Colombia's tax base and narrow its yawning fiscal deficit, Caballero said it eliminated one of the key incentives for investment in stocks.
"The measures will undoubtedly affect local investment funds holdings and individuals who are active in the stock market and obliged to pay income tax," one Boggota-based broker said.
"To a certain extent that was reflected in today's low volumes," he said.

Although the measure has no direct effect on foreign funds, brokers said fund managers were jittery because of sudden changes in rules of the game in Colombia and the possibility that economic sanctions would be clamped on the country in March, when U.S. President Bill Clinton must certify whether it is cooperating in the anti-drug war.

Movers Monday included tobacco company Coltabaco, which fell 5.41 percent in Medellin to end at 3,500 pesos per share. Blue-chip Banco Ganadero closed down 0.33 percent in Bogota at 296 pesos a share while brewer Bavaria edged up 0.33 percent.
